standard_prerequisites.name: Yoneda's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-yoneda (canonical Stacks tag 001P); invoked at proof line 1192
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a complex with the prescribed representing terms and maps exists uniquely up to the displayed description.

core_obligations: Identify the terms: for each tuple of indices the discussion preceding the statement gives Hom_{O_X}((j_{i_0...i_p})_{p!}O_{U_{i_0...i_p}}, F) = F(U_{i_0...i_p}), so the direct sum of those sheaves represents the functor F -> the product of the F(U_{i_0...i_p}) (proof lines 1172-1191).

Apply Yoneda: by Yoneda's lemma there is a chain complex K(U)_bullet with exactly those terms, and its differentials are the ones displayed in the statement (with the alternating sign times the canonical map) (proof lines 1192-1195).

Conclude the identification: maps of complexes from K(U)_bullet into F are thus the same as the degreewise product of the values of F on the intersections with the Cech differential, which is the Cech complex, functorially in F (proof lines 1174-1195).
proof_roadmap: Use the representing property of the extension-by-zero sheaves to identify the Hom groups with the values of F on the intersections (proof lines 1173-1180).
Conclude that the direct sum represents the product functor, and apply Yoneda to obtain the complex with the displayed terms (proof lines 1181-1192).
Read off that the differentials are the displayed alternating maps, which gives the identification with the Cech complex (proof lines 1193-1195).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs a chain complex K(U)_bullet of presheaves of O_X-modules out of the extension-by-zero sheaves of the structure sheaf on the finite intersections of a covering, and identifies the complex of maps from it into any presheaf F with the Cech complex of F, functorially (statement lines 1139-1169). The proof rests on one representing property, Hom((j_{i_0...i_p})_{p!}O_{U_{i_0...i_p}}, F) = F(U_{i_0...i_p}), which makes the direct sum represent the product functor, after which Yoneda produces the complex and its differentials with the alternating signs (proof lines 1173-1195). The author's phrase 'It is a simple matter to see that the maps are as given' leaves that last check implicit and is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: one representing property plus Yoneda, no constructions beyond the complex itself.
